The wave is fully contained before 24038: restricting the window to [18400,24038] reproduces all 9 closures identically (step_04), so the last closing interaction is t = 24038 (triangle 338-1244-1585, wedge at 23292).

Part 2: A time-respecting route exists from 244 to 343 with all inter-hop waits <= 600: 244->1782 (25038), ->1452 (25322), ->1729 (25598), ->343 (25752); max wait actually used is 284 (step_03).

Coupling: the route's first hop at t=25038 begins 1000 time units after the wave finished at 24038, comfortably inside the 4000-unit admissible period; the route is independently confirmed to lie entirely within [24038,28038] (step_05). Critically, the route does NOT exist before the wave ends — reachability under the same 600-unit constraint in [18400,24038] fails, reaching only 4 nodes (step_08) — so the ordering is genuine rather than an artifact of a route that was always available.

Confounder controls: this is not a volume or popularity effect. The window holds 2313 events over 1573 active nodes with repeat_ratio 0.0009, i.e. a sparse, near-simple graph (step_01). The route's carriers are all low-degree — 244, 343, 1782, 1452, 1729 have only 2-4 events each (step_07) — and none appear among the 10 most active nodes, which are dominated by 463 (89 events) and 1959 (36) (step_06). The path therefore reflects specific ordered timing, not hub traffic.
